question: What does adopting the mattpocock/skills pack cost tezgah - in always-on context, in router-line extractability, and in test/gate conflicts - and which of its mechanisms, if any, earn an arm-bench effect block?

evaluation.metric: (a) router yield: of the upstream 38 SKILL.md, the count whose description returns a non-trigger line through tezgah's own skill_description() (bin/tezgah-setup:693-730), classified by the extractor's own rule ^(Also )?[Uu]se\b; (b) always-on cost: bytes by the installer's own formula sum(len(name)+len(description)+8) per corpus (bin/tezgah-setup:1754-1755), measured against CORE and CONTRACT as the scale, never summed across scopes; (c) conflict verdicts: the number of executable guards that fire on the pack's verbatim text, split into mechanical (a test or gate returns a verdict) and policy (a rule a human must remember).
evaluation.baseline: (a) control 14/14 shipped tezgah skills return a trigger-bearing line - tests/test_setup.py:589-609 pins the two core ones - and the extractor's documented fallback is the opening sentence; (b) the report's own metadata row recomputed at HEAD over the 14 names, plus CORE 13483 B and CONTRACT 35860 B read from hooks/tezgah_policy.py; (c) 0 failing tests at HEAD and 0 attribution denials for the pack's mandated line.
evaluation.locked_at: 2026-09-21T00:00:00+0300 (written before any probe ran; the protocols under experiments/*/protocol.md were committed before their results, and the evaluation - metric, baseline, locked_at - has not changed since. The hypotheses list below was EXTENDED after E4 ran and H4's entry quotes E4's numbers; that is a later edit to this file, not a post-hoc criterion, and the session events record it.)

environment.no_model_in_the_loop: every probe is deterministic and reads files; no model call is made in this round

hypotheses: H1 router yield (CONFIRMED): the pack's 22 user-invoked skills carry a human-facing description with the trigger list stripped by design, so tezgah's extractor falls back to the opening sentence for at least 13 of the 38 upstream SKILL.md. Measured: 22 of 38 fall back, all 22 user-invoked, against 14 of 14 for the shipped control (C01).

H2 always-on cost (REFUTED on the byte prediction, CONFIRMED on the reference): the upstream 38-skill metadata row is at least 2x tezgah's 14-skill row, and the pack's craft reference is smaller than CONTRACT. Measured: 6180 B against 9000 B, 0.69x, the opposite direction (C02); the craft reference is 13515 B, 0.38x CONTRACT (C06b).

H3 conflict split (CONFIRMED, with the corpus qualification): the pack's conflicts are mostly policy-level - the floating tag lives in its READMEs rather than its SKILL.md bodies, and the mandated AI-attribution line passes the attribution gate because the anchor set holds 'generated with' and not 'generated by AI'. Measured: 0 of 38 bodies and 1 of 66 markdown files carry the float (C03c) and the mandated line is allowed while the Co-Authored-By control is denied (C04). The qualification the battery adds: the float IS a mechanical conflict the moment the text sits in a body (C05), so what keeps it policy-level is the corpus, not the absence of a rule.

H4 effect block (CLOSED, NEGATIVE): the clause ran in round 3 (3eb8b9f8, $1.0997, 300 usable rows) after two infrastructure failures (C11, C13). It changed nothing measurable: P2 falsified by its own wording (false-completion 1.000 on both armed arms, one labelled failed run each), P3 confirmed (94.0% against 89.0%, intervals overlapping), Stop-rule refusals identical at 74. The corpus, not the clause, is the binding limit (C14, C15).
